articles.title: Control Resonant gets tough, but gives you the tools to deal with it
articles.summary: Control Resonant’s generous assist mode lets you tweak settings to more easily experience the game’s world and story.
articles.body: Control Resonant isn’t an easy game. At any given moment while exploring vast open areas where you’re sometimes leaping from wall to wall to ceiling, you may be surrounded by swarms of otherworldly enemies trying to crush you into the ground. It can be a lot, especially when enemies sometimes take a long time to take down. I died often. But whenever I got to a point where I was starting to feel frustrated, I didn’t have to suffer for too long; thanks to Resonant’s generous assist mode, I often tweaked the game’s settings to give me an edge so that I could keep on trucking through the game’s weird world. The assist mode is accessible from Control Resonant’s pause menu. You can tweak things like how much damage you give and take or how generous of a window you have for pulling off dodges, and you can even give yourself immortality or the ability to pull off one-hit kills. There are also a few presets that are a bit like traditional difficulty options if you don’t want to get too deep into messing with the sliders. While the game encourages you to try playing with assist mode disabled, there’s no penalty to flipping it on, and you don’t even need to reload your game if you do so. [Image: I started using assist mode quite early. Initially, you don’t have many combat abilities or passive skills to make fighting easier, and I was regularly getting my clock cleaned. But with a few small adjustments in assist mode, I made myself just a little bit more powerful while not completely removing any challenge, which kept fights engaging at a pace that felt right to me. After a few hours of leveling up, I noticed I was starting to coast, so I turned assist mode off to bring the difficulty back up. I found myself toggling assist mode in different ways as I played. Resonant throws a lot of bad guys at you, and I sometimes found the combat to be pretty boring. But instead of resigning myself to slogging through frustrating fights that blocked me from seeing the trippy story beats and locations that I love about Remedy games, I’d adjust some assist mode settings, take out the enemies in my way, and move on to the good stuff. This was a particularly good approach for Resonant’s bosses, which are awe-inspiring spectacles but feature giant health bars; I’d usually start a fight with assist mode disabled and incrementally tweak settings in my favor every time I died so that I could still feel the thrill of a fight without completely eliminating the challenge. Assist mode was also great for more efficiently tackling Resonant’s sprawling maps, which are littered with secrets and quests. In one area, I had to track down a bunch of chunks of weird mold that protagonist Dylan felt compelled to eat. (It’s gross, but it makes sense in context, I promise.) When I first understood the scope of the mission, I wasn’t looking forward to it; I figured the quest waypoints would all be guarded by hordes of enemies that I didn’t really want to deal with. I just wanted to learn about the mold. But by flipping on immortality and one-hit kills, I blasted through the boring fights so that I could more quickly get to the mold and the narrative reveals that followed. When I got to the (satisfyingly stomach-turning) boss at the end of the quest, I turned off my superpowers so I could take it on. Control Resonant has a little too much bloat; there are too many enemies wandering the maps and too many open-world activities to sort through. The game’s combat isn’t interesting enough, like in a FromSoftware title or Capcom’s recent Onimusha: Way of the Sword, to make suffering feel worth it. It also, like the original Control, suffers from big difficulty spikes. Remedy patched an assist mode into Control after launch, and with Resonant, it’s including one right from the start. The feature let me set my own pace so that I could see the best parts of the game, which is filled with mind-bending set-pieces and twists, on my own terms.

articles.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered Global Release Times Confirmed by CD Projekt
articles.summary: CD Projekt has confirmed the global release times for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered. Here's when you can play in your region.
articles.body:
CD Projekt has confirmed the global release times for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered .

As detailed in a social media post , The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered comes out on September 29 at 12pm in Poland, where CD Projekt is based. All other release times across the globe are tied to this CET release. So, if you’re wondering if it’s worth keeping the day free (book off from work, perhaps?), the farther west you are, the earlier the game goes live.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered launches across PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and Nintendo Switch 2, but it’s also a free upgrade for those who own the base game. The remaster will also be sold on PC via Battle.net for the first time. There's pre-purchase for Switch 2 and Battle.net (those are the only new versions of the game, as The Witcher 3 didn't exist before on those two platforms). GOG, Steam, Epic, Xbox and PlayStation are getting the remaster as an update, so there's no preload on those platforms.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered Screenshots

Expect a slew of upgrades and enhancements to visuals, performance, gameplay, and more. There’s enhanced combat, improved traversal and movement, new witcher signs effects, revamped mount handling, enhanced monster behaviors, a skill tree revamp, transmogrification, expanded photo mode, and new finishers. The launch precedes the arrival of Songs of the Past, The Witcher 3's third expansion, due in 2027.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered global release times:

This week, The Witcher 3 fans reacted to an official comparison clip featuring a snippet of side-by-side gameplay from the original game and the remaster, with some saying the new version actually looks worse. In the clip, you can see Geralt casting Igni on a group of drowners in the swamp. While the new version of the game has much greater detail on Geralt's armor, along with much more defined water, the reflections seem to be divisive.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: 'One of the Very Few Games I'm Going to Be Buying': Control Resonant Has Leaked, But There's a Push Among Some Pirates to Pay For It Anyway
articles.summary: Video game pirates appear to be making a rare effort to pay for Control Resonant, in order to support its developer Remedy.
articles.body:
Video game pirates appear to be making a rare effort to pay for Control Resonant , in order to support its developer Remedy.

Control Resonant launched today for PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S and, somewhat inevitably, cracked copies of the game are already circulating online. But among the threads pointing people to illegal copies, there appears to be a concerted effort among some video game fans to support Control Resonant's development team.

Remedy is well known as the maker of Max Payne, Alan Wake, Control, and Quantum Break, but its games often find relatively niche audiences. Fans of the studio love Remedy's offbeat stories and often dark humor, as well as its typically high quality bar. But its past few launches have struggled to sell, with Alan Wake 2 taking over a year to turn a profit, and new content for multiplayer experiment FBC: Firebreak ended in less than a year.

Control Resonant - June 2026 Screenshots

In response to fan uncertainty over Remedy's future, and a growing sense that the studio really needs Control Resonant to be a success, there are now numerous messages on game piracy forums and reddit from pirates suggesting they will make an exception for this game, and actually open up their wallet.

"One of the very few games I'm going to be buying, Remedy are on the brink of bankruptcy, this is their make or break title, I love their games and gotta do what I can to keep them afloat," wrote one fan.

"I wasn't planning to buy it but now I feel like I should," reads one reply. "I like Remedy. They do good games."

"Yeah same here," reads another response. "Remedy makes amazing games, that's a studio that deserve my money, and I hope they continue to make more games."

"I feel like this is one of the games which you shouldn't pirate if you can," reads a similar comment on a separate discussion thread. "Remedy makes unique, innovative games, they need this funding."

However, not everyone agreed. "That's great idea, but this is a piracy reddit," reads one response. "Agreed, I gotta eat so this is being pirated but they do deserve success," reads another.

Still, there's a presiding sense that of all the games to avoid pirating, Control Resonant stands out. "I mean if you're going to compensate the team outside of Steam for playing their game that's one thing, but pretending that because you need to eat gives you the right to steal a video game is ridiculous."

And, if you are in any doubt over whether the game is your cup of tea, IGN's Control Resonant review is here to answer that question for you. "Even when combat's sharp edge eventually dulls, Control Resonant is a great addition to the Remedyverse," we wrote, awarding the game an 8/10. "While its story follows a more standard framework, its gravitational pull is in the inventive world built around it and the humanization that grounds the paranatural intrigue."

In August, Jean-Charles Gaudechon, installed as CEO of Remedy in March, said Control Resonant had 1.5 million wishlists across PC and consoles, and was among the top three pre-ordered PlayStation games in the U.S., Germany, and Brazil.

"We position Control Resonant as a must-have day-one purchase while also building Control into a lasting franchise," Gaudechon said at the time . "In a competitive autumn window, we believe the distinctiveness and quality of the game will make it stand out. Control Resonant will be available across all major platforms from day one and is priced attractively for an AAA title. Combined with the release window becoming slightly less crowded since our original reveal, we remain confident in our positioning."

Other than Control Resonant, Remedy continues its lengthy development work on the Max Payne 1 & 2 remakes, which are still listed as in production. The company also has an unannounced "new project" which it said had reached "production readiness," without providing further detail. Is this early work on an Alan Wake 3, another Control game, or something brand new? We'll have to wait and see, though Remedy certainly doesn't sound like it's giving up on Alan just yet.

"We have two established own franchises, Control and Alan Wake, which are linked through the Remedy Connected Universe," Gaudechon concluded, looking to the future. "Remedy will self-publish upcoming games, in which Remedy owns the IP. Growing and expanding the two franchises will be a key part of our future. In addition, we work with a partner franchise Max Payne, originally created by Remedy."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: WonderPaws, a Cozy Life Sim Set in a City of Animals, Announced for PC
articles.summary: Developer Lilith's Cat Paw Latte has announced WonderPaws, a very cozy and very adorable multiplayer life sim in which you can build your own life in Paw City, a busy borough bustling with anthropomorphic animal life. It's in development for PC.
articles.body:
Developer Lilith's Cat Paw Latte has announced WonderPaws, a very cozy and very adorable multiplayer life sim in which you can build your own life in Paw City, a busy borough bustling with anthropomorphic animal life. It's in development for PC.

The aim is to make WonderPaws a totally stress-free cozy game where you can shop, socialize, befriend animals and other players – all with your Paw Pal. The cities designs are inspired by animal habitats, such as wider avenues for elephants and clear tubes for hamsters to commute through. You can even move into a downtown apartment and enjoy a view of the city.

Oh, and you can even turn into a Paw Pal yourself if you so choose. WonderPaws is due to launch on PC and mobile in 2027. Wishlist it on Steam if you're interested.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Early Amazon Prime Day Deals Drop on MTG Final Fantasy, Marvel, and TMNT Sets in the UK
articles.summary: Score early Amazon UK Prime Day savings on Magic: The Gathering sets, featuring up to 28% off TMNT, discounted Marvel boxes, and Final Fantasy Commander decks.
articles.body:
Prime Day is getting closer, and as sure as death and taxes, Amazon’s sales event is likely to feature some great deals on Magic: The Gathering products.

The long-running card game gets regular price cuts in the UK, but they’re never quite as good as the savings in the US. Thankfully, there are still some worth being aware of, including pre-Prime Day deals on sets from 2026 and the popular Final Fantasy Commander precons.

While some of these require a Prime membership, others are available to all, so let us know if you pick anything up!

The Best Pre-Prime Day Deals On Magic: The Gathering

Marvel Legends x Magic: The Gathering Figures (Various)

It feels strange to think that Magic’s first Universes Beyond set of 2026 was Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.

The humble set was smaller than the likes of Marvel’s Super Heroes, and not as fantasy-adjacent as The Hobbit, but it still had some neat reprints and a Turtle in every pack.

You can save 28% on a bundle including nine Play Boosters, a handy card box, an alt-art card, and a special die. It’s now £43.80, down from £60.99 at Amazon .

Sticking within 2026 sets, there are a few Marvel Super Heroes sets on sale, too. The big draw for many will be the Marvel Super Heroes Draft Night box, now £87.01 down from £112.45.

This box includes 12 Play Boosters, 90 Lands, and the all-important (and increasingly tough to find) Collector Booster. The idea is that you play draft to determine who wins it, but given that one pack makes up £40 of the value here, you’re actually getting a pretty great deal .

You can also save 29% on a Scene Box with Heroes United , offering a series of borderless cards that combine to make an image (and playable versions of them, thankfully).

It also includes three Play Boosters, so you’re getting plenty of bang for your buck. It’s £24.99 right now, down from £34.99 - this is one I may grab, especially since it’s at its lowest-ever price.

As we pointed out last week , Avengers Assemble is a fantastic Commander deck, and it’s still seeing a 10% discount , while you can also save on the Marvel Legends series of action figures that come with an exclusive foil trading card.

My recommendation is Anti-Venom, Horrifying Healer - I’m still trying to work him into a Commander deck. It’s £33.98, a discount of 15% from the RRP.

Last but not least, all four Commander decks from the (excellent) Final Fantasy set are seeing discounts. While prices kept climbing at launch, it feels like they’re still being printed, and now they’re much more affordable and still fantastic.

Every deck can be found at £46.98, a slim 6% discount from the usual price of £49.97 for Revival Trance, but a much steeper 20% saving from the £58.45 that Counter Blitz, Limit Break, and Scions & Spellcraft would usually set you back.

For more on Magic: The Gathering, check out all we know about the latest on Monster Hunter x Secret Lair , and which Marvel sets we predict will appear soon .

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: New Clayface Trailer Resists the Urge to Reveal His Final Form, Which Is Exactly How It Should Be
articles.summary: DC Studios has released the final Clayface trailer, which does not, thankfully, reveal his final form.
articles.body:
DC Studios has released the final Clayface trailer, which does not, thankfully, reveal his final form.

Speaking to Entertainment Weekly in the summer, Clayface actor Tom Rhys Harries teased what fans can expect to see of his character’s final form when they watch the R-rated body horror movie.

“It’s been a year since I saw that thing being built out. I can’t wait for people to see it,” he says. “I’m constantly in awe of the huge creative machinery that goes into making a film like this, and how talented everybody on board is, and how lucky I felt to be a part of that in any way.”

Then, speaking to Empire magazine this week, Rhys Harries teased Clayface’s final form further, saying: “It’s f***ing sick!”

While Clayface trailers have shown how Matt Hagen becomes Clayface, with his face melting and, in one particularly disturbing shot, his eyelids fusing together, DC Studios have resisted the urge to show the Gotham bad guy in all his glory. Fans of the character from the comics and animated shows probably have an idea of what to expect here, but seeing Clayface in live-action will surely be a thrill for all.

Fans are completely on board with DC Studios holding Clayface’s final form back, as am I. The last thing you want is for the movie’s big reveal to be spoiled before the movie itself even comes out. I suspect we’ll see the final form at the end of the film as part of a setup for the character’s introduction into the wider DC Universe. Where Clayface will then appear in live-action is unknown, but you’d like to think James Gunn has a plan for the character, given he’s got his own movie.

The DCU is currently trundling forward, with the final two episodes of Lanterns out soon. We then have Clayface hitting theaters on October 23. Man of Tomorrow, Gunn’s Superman follow-up, comes out next summer. Upcoming HBO show The People v. Gorilla Grodd, which is filming now, follows.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

Beyond that, we have no other confirmed DCU projects in active production, let alone with release windows. But we know there are plans for Batman, Swamp Thing, and Wonder Woman movies eventually.

As for this new Clayface trailer, there's a shot of Hagen suffocating someone inside his stomach, and you can see the head of his hapless victom protruding from his lower back (that's a bad way to go). But we also get Clayface's final form teased, briefly, at the end of the trailer via the shadow of what looks like his growing arm, his bulbous hand, and the slow rise of the monster himself.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Domhnall Gleeson Would Have Loved to Have Delved Deeper Into the 'Bitterness' of Star Wars' General Hux
articles.summary: Domhnall Gleeson says he would have loved to have delved deeper into the "bitterness" of his Star Wars villain General Hux, before Rise of Skywalker's twist ended the character's story in surprising fashion.
articles.body:
Domhnall Gleeson says he would have loved to have delved deeper into the "bitterness" of his Star Wars villain General Hux, before Rise of Skywalker's twist ended the character's story in surprising fashion.

Warning! Spoilers for The Rise of Skywalker follow...

Hux appears in all three of the Star Wars sequel trilogy films, beginning as a downtrodden sidekick for Kylo Ren, and ending up as a secret Rebel spy. Unfortunately for Hux, his last minute change of heart ultimately spells his doom — as he is quickly discovered and killed off.

It's an abrupt reveal and an even swifter demise for one of the few characters to appear in all of the sequels, though no less messy than anything else in the disappointing Star Wars Episode 9: Rise of Skywalker . And while Hux's sideplot is hardly the most pressing storyline, even Gleeson has admitted he'd previously hoped for more.

Star Wars The Rise of Skywalker: The Best Easter Eggs, Nods, References, Callbacks, Cameos and Homages

"Speaking genuinely, it would have been nice to go into the real bitterness at the heart of him," Gleeson told Liv Marks . "In a quiet way, just to find a couple of quiet moments with him, where it's not performative, where the real danger of him comes across.

"A kicked dog will end up attacking someone," he continued, "and he is a kicked dog by the end of that sort of stuff. So I would have loved to go into that stuff but, spoiler alert, I got shot in the chest by Richard E. Grant."

As part of the same interview, Gleeson said his big speech to the First Order troops was one of his easiest scenes as he knew how to fully lean into the character at such a dramatic moment. At the same time, Gleeson said his corridor conversations with Adam Driver's petulant Kylo Ren needed to worked on in the moment, in order to ensure the pair walked the fine line to make the scenes work.

Perhaps there's room for more Hux in the wider Star Wars universe of spinoff books, comics and video games? I for one would be glad to see more of Gleeson's glowering baddie, working to quietly undermine the First Order. It'd be better than what we actually got in Rise of Skywalker!

Next up for the Star Wars franchise — and sadly without Hux — Disney will finally return to the ongoing exploits of Ahsoka in a second season of Disney+ TV episodes next year. Then there's Ryan Gosling's Star Wars: Starfighter, headed to theaters in May 2027. Hopes are high for both of these, after the middling response to this year's The Mandalorian and Grogu.

Image credit: Mert Alper Dervis /Anadolu via Getty Images.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Getting a $400 Collector's Set That Doesn't Include the Game
articles.summary: GTA 6 is getting a $400 collector's set filled with Vice City-themed goodies, but it won't include a copy of the game.
articles.body:
GTA 6 is getting a $400 collector's set filled with Vice City-themed goodies, but it won't include a copy of the game.

Rockstar Games has announced a collector's set for GTA 6 known as GTA 6: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection. The $400 box will not include a copy of the game, but will include a bunch of premium merchandise, including a pair of Oakley sunglasses, a bobblehead, a hat, pins, stickers, and a variety of other items themed after the game's crime-ridden paradise. The set is available to pre-order now through Rockstar's website and will release on November 19.

You can view the full list of items below with images.

GTA 6 Vice City Collection Collector's Set Items

Everything Included in the GTA 6: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection

6” figure of Macca the Gator with stash compartment

Matte black GTAVI Oakley® Frogskins™ sunglasses with Prizm Sapphire lenses

New Era® 9FORTY A-Frame snapback hat with Vice City Leonida embellishments

Leonida Keys enamel pin set in a custom metal tin

Double-sided souvenir poster showcasing the full Leonida landscape

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

One interesting thing to note here is that previous GTA and Red Dead games have historically always included a physical map in the standard edition of the game. We've reached out to Rockstar to see if the map is included in the boxed copies of GTA 6 or if players will have to shell out a few hundred bucks to get one.

With that said, this is a pretty pricey box set, but at least the items are of high-quality. By partnering with brands like Oakley for these items, it does ensure that these aren't cheap gas station quality sunglasses that will fall apart on you in a few months. You can also likely expect that these will sell out rather quickly and be resold on eBay for absurd prices. GTA 6-themed shirts were given away at Tokyo Game Show earlier this month and have been popping up online for hundreds of dollars .

Rockstar's foot appears to be on the gas now as launch is just under two months away. After years of prolonged silence, GTA 6 has had non-stop news since June when pre-orders opened for the game. There has also been a new marketing beat every week since the gameplay reveal at the end of August , with the reveal of limited edition DualSense controllers and an album comprised of original music from major artists . Rockstar also recently installed a massive "Welcome to Vice City" sign in on the Miami Heat's arena in Florida, which reportedly cost the company nearly $1 million .

It's currently unclear if or when there will be another look at the game, but one last big trailer before launch doesn't seem out of the question. Some have speculated one will arrive in mid-October, possibly timed to the start of the NBA regular season. We'll have to wait and see what happens, but it seems clear that the marketing machine is only just getting started.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: How Best Buy Became a Hidden Haven for Authentic Pokémon TCG Drops at MSRP Prices With Anti-Scalper Queues
articles.summary: Looking for authentic Pokémon TCG cards? Best Buy offers a wide selection, MSRP pricing, and strong bot protection to beat the scalpers.
articles.body:
Editor's Note: This article is sponsored by Best Buy. If you buy through our links, IGN may earn an affiliate commission. Learn more .

Collecting Pokémon cards has been a favorite pastime for millions of people for decades at this point, but in recent years, getting your hands on new drops has gotten increasingly frustrating. They’re cleaned out by bots almost instantly, scalpers charge double the price, and third-party marketplaces are full of resealed or weighed packs.

When you think of Best Buy , you probably associate them with TVs, laptops, and electronics in general. But what’s gone under the radar is that they’ve become a fantastic option for buying Pokémon cards thanks to huge stock, MSRP pricing, anti-scalper protections, early access, and authenticity guarantees.

If you’re a devoted Pokémon card collector, you probably already know that most stores that carry them have pretty limited variety. You can get a few booster packs and maybe a couple other options, but that’s pretty much it.

Best Buy might surprise you with how huge its selection is, including from the latest expansions. From the Mega Evolution Pitch Black series that launched with 120 cards in July, there are sleeved booster packs , booster bundles , and Elite Trainer Boxes .

That’s just scratching the surface of what’s available. Best Buy also carries previous expansions as well as coveted Ultra-Premium Collections (like Mega Charizard X Ex ) and other collector’s items (like the Pokemon Center Tohoku Special Box ). There are pages upon pages of available packs and boxes.

Life is full of annoying things, but near the top of the list is getting excited about an upcoming drop, only to have bots steal everything out from under you. Seeing “sold out” under a new release seconds after it goes on sale is a special kind of soul-crushing. Best Buy combats this with invitations, digital queues, strict purchase limits, and surprise drops.

Particularly popular upcoming releases will allow you to request launch day access ahead of time by signing into your Best Buy account and clicking “Invite to Purchase” on the item page. Best Buy will then alert a set number of people that they’ve been selected and provide a secure link where they have 24 hours to complete their purchase.

If a drop doesn’t have invites beforehand, you can use the Best Buy app to enter a waiting room on launch day. Everyone is limited to one purchase, which prevents a bot from swooping in and buying everything at once. It doesn’t guarantee every person will get what they want or that no scalpers will get in, since that’s unfortunately impossible. However, it evens the playing field to give real humans a chance to check out safely.

There are also sudden surprise drops that will go unannounced until they’re already underway, giving you the chance to spontaneously grab new cards. You have to be quick on these drops though, so follow Best Buy’s social channels to see announcements and jump on them immediately.

If you follow the prices of packs and boxes closely, you might have noticed that some shops and retailers will jack up the price on a set that has a lot of buzz. They’ll refer to this as “dynamic pricing,” but we call it a “hype tax.” Best Buy has declared that they won’t do that, they always stick to MSRP. So if a box normally retails for $49.99, that’s how much they’ll charge for it.

Nobody is going to complain about not paying extra money. For major collectors, that can save you hundreds of dollars a year, so that’s an obvious benefit of the guarantee. But it also helps with peace of mind, knowing you’re not going to get an unwelcome surprise once a new set goes on sale.

My Best Buy Plus is a membership program that costs $29.99 per year that brings benefits like members-only prices on certain products, an extended return window, and free expedited shipping. But the most relevant benefit when it comes to Pokémon card collectors is exclusive early access to TCG pre-orders.

If you have a My Best Buy Plus account, you’ll be able to access pre-orders before the general public, which can make the difference in getting the item you want. This still isn’t a guarantee that you’ll be successful, since it’s based on things like the amount of stock available and the level of demand. But it can give you a leg up.

Considering the steep difference in price between MSRP and the resale market, getting in on one pre-order you would have otherwise missed could cover the cost of a yearly membership. Only you can know if a membership is right for you, but if you make proper use of its benefits, you can end up saving more than you spend.

Another reality of our increasingly digital world is the risk you take having valuable things shipped to your home. Have you ever waited for a shipment like it’s a gift on Christmas morning, then had it arrive with the box dented and contents inside scratched? Or even worse, have you gotten a notification that your package has been delivered, only to get home and find that someone stole it off your porch? If you haven’t, trust us: it really sucks.

Best Buy has a hybrid purchase system that can help, giving you the convenience of shopping online but the reliability of picking up in person. Waiting in the queue, checkout, and payment can all be handled on your phone or computer, then just select in-store pickup and the location you want to pick up from.

Your local store will hold your order for up to five days, so you’re assured that your item will stay safe and secure until you’re able to pick it up. Of course, this means you need a store close enough to be able to visit in person, but with more than 1,000 Best Buy stores across North America, most people should have access to one.

How to Guarantee You Get Factory Sealed Items

Shopping online with big retailers can sometimes be confusing about who is actually selling an item, since third-party sellers can get mixed into search results without being clearly labeled. That can mean you’re at risk of buying fake cards or resealed packs from a seller you don’t know.

Best Buy also has third-party sellers, so you still need to be vigilant and make sure you verify who you’re buying from, but that’s very easy to do. Just look above the “Add to Cart” button on the item page and make sure it says “Sold by Best Buy” instead of “Sold & shipped by [seller name].”

If you don’t even want to see items being sold by third-party sellers, you can easily do that too. When you filter your search results, simply click the “Store Pickup” option. Since it’s impossible for third-party sellers to allow in-store pickup, this ensures all listings you see are actually from Best Buy.

All items bought directly from Best Buy are guaranteed to be factory sealed straight from The Pokémon Company, so as long as you pay attention to what you’re buying, you can be 100% certain of their authenticity and condition.

All of these features combine to make Best Buy a worthy option for buying new Pokémon cards. There’s a huge selection to choose from, you know you won’t have to pay above MSRP, there are bot protections in place, membership options allow for early access, and it’s easy to ensure you’re getting authentic items.

So if you’re a long-time collector who’s sick of dealing with scalpers, you’ve been scammed into buying fake cards before, or you’re just looking for a place you know will have the next big drop, Best Buy should be your first stop.

Corey DeMoss is a Custom Content Writer for IGN who has covered titles big and small from all around the world. He has nearly 20 years of experience as a writer and editor.

articles.title: 'I Don’t Think Starfield Was Anywhere Near Successful Enough to Do a Starfield 2' – Former Bethesda Dev Casts Doubt on Sequel
articles.summary: Former Bethesda Lead Systems Designer Kurt Kuhlmann spoke to FRVR, and when he was asked about a potential Starfield sequel, he told the outlet "I don’t think Starfield was anywhere near successful enough to do a Starfield 2."
articles.body:
Bethesda is still hard at work on new DLC for Starfield , but you probably shouldn't expect a sequel anytime soon.

Former Bethesda Lead Systems Designer Kurt Kuhlmann spoke to FRVR , and when he was asked about a potential Starfield sequel, he told the outlet: "I don’t think Starfield was anywhere near successful enough to do a Starfield 2."

That's not too surprising, as the game has been massively divisive since it came out, despite getting a mostly-positive review from us here at IGN. Our reviewer Dan Stapleton said: "Starfield has a lot of forces working against it, but eventually the allure of its expansive roleplaying quests and respectable combat make its gravitational pull difficult to resist."

Kuhlmann then goes on to reminisce on the ambition of Starfield, and how a sequel could have done something great, saying "It’s, in a way, too bad, because I think with the lessons learned on Starfield, a Starfield 2 could have been much closer to the game that Todd [Howard] had [in mind]." Starfield has improved a lot since it first came out, and it's still has improvements down the pipeline, but it's pretty clear that it fell short of Todd Howard's ambitions ahead of its release.

Still, Howard reiterated Starfield's support back in July, when he put out a statement saying: "As we enter Year 3, we'll continue expanding the Settled Systems with new stories, targeted gameplay improvements, and additional updates, while preparing for the launch of new Starborn content next year." It's possible that despite Kuhlmann's predictions, these updates will be able to turn Starfield around, but it's unlikely.

Instead, it seems like Bethesda is entirely focused on getting The Elder Scrolls VI out the door (even if it's still likely a couple years away), and Obsidian has been tapped to develop a new Fallout game . Even if a new Starfield game was somehow in the works, it'd be years before we ever heard about it. It's probably safe to assume that it's not going to happen any time in the near future.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Beyond Good & Evil 2 Is Still Alive, and Just Added an Assassin's Creed Shadows Writer
articles.summary: Beyond Good & Evil 2 is still in development, and just added another writer to its team.
articles.body:
Beyond Good & Evil 2 is still in development, and just added another writer to its team.

18 years on from its initial announcement and a decade on from its re-announcement at E3 2016, Ubisoft is still plugging away on its sci-fi fantasy sequel — though there's still no word on when the game will actually release.

That said, work is clearly continuing. Just this week, Ubisoft Bordeaux's lead writer/associate narrative director Rik Godwin confirmed via social media that he had joined the project a few months ago, working in a support/consultant role.

Founded in 2017, Ubisoft Bordeaux has typically acted as a support studio for other projects, though led work on Assassin's Creed Mirage and most recently released Claws of Awaji, the one and only expansion for Assassin's Creed Shadows. Geographically, it makes sense that Bordeaux-based personnel are helping out on Beyond Good & Evil 2, which is led by Ubisoft Montpellier, situated to the south.

It's another intriguing development for Beyond Good & Evil 2 for those who have been tracking its extremely slow progress (yet progress nonetheless) in recent years, ever since it gained a new creative director, Fawzi Mesmar to steady its ship. The last while has subsequently seen work coalesce once more, with the sequel's characters given intriguing cameos in the new Beyond Good & Evil 20th Anniversary Edition , cementing a sense that the project now had a firm direction.

Then there's the fact that the project survived Ubisoft's existential reshuffle of projects, brands and development studios earlier this year — despite various other games falling by the wayside (Prince of Persia: Sands of Time Remake, we'll never forget you.)

"Needless to say, I am saddened by the cancellations that has affected my colleagues in other parts of Ubisoft and the industry," Mesmar said at the time. "I urge everyone — myself included — to offer support whenever and however they can during these times. We remain committed and focused on delivering a remarkable game for our players to enjoy."

Inexplicable as it may be, but there remains a sense that Beyond Good & Evil 2 actually still may release one day, having got this far. Exactly how it will look and whether Ubisoft ultimately chooses to keep the game's name remains to be seen. But here's hoping we will indeed see the answers to these questions, sooner rather than later.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: AMC’s NYCC Lineup Features The Walking Dead, Mayfair Witches, and More - Exclusive
articles.summary: AMC has revealed its full New York Comic Con lineup, featuring exclusive panels and sneak peeks for The Walking Dead: Daryl Dixon, Mayfair Witches, and more.
articles.body:
When New York Comic Con kicks off on October 8, AMC is slated to be there in full force with witches, zombies, plenty of screams, and more.

Ahead of the epic fan convention, IGN can exclusively reveal that AMC Global Media’s New York Comic Con lineup will include fan-favorite shows like The Walking Dead: Daryl Dixon, Anne Rice’s Mayfair Witches, and The Boulet Brothers’ Dragula, along with new shows like Kill Jackie and YAGA. Panels are slated to include special previews, in-depth conversations, first looks, and more.

Oscar-winner Catherine Zeta-Jones will join showrunner, writer and executive producer Tom Butterworth and executive producer Peter Lawson for a special conversation about the new AMC+ revenge thriller featuring exclusive sneak peeks at upcoming episodes.

Kill Jackie premieres October 2 on AMC+ and follows Jackie Price (Zeta-Jones), who “has been living a luxurious existence for the last twenty years – traveling the world, selling fine art and, above all, trying to stay anonymous after escaping a dangerous past as an international drug smuggler. But just as life starts to feel a little boring, it takes a sudden lethal turn when she discovers a squad of the world’s most terrifying hitmen has been hired to kill her.”

Cast members Carrie-Anne Moss, Noah Reid, and Clark Backo are joined by showrunner, writer and executive producer Kat Sandler and executive producer Mackenzie Donaldson for a panel discussion featuring a sneak preview of the new AMC+ series.

Based on the play by Sandler, YAGA premieres October 23 on AMC+ and “reimagines the Slavic folk tale of the Baba Yaga witch as a contemporary mystery thriller. It follows Rapp (Reid), a private investigator who arrives in a small coastal town to investigate the disappearance of a young heir to a powerful fishery, Henry Park (Hudson Williams). Rapp finds himself at odds with an apprehensive local detective, Carson (Backo), a charismatic university professor, Katherine (Moss) and a labyrinth of enigmatic suspects, secret lives and ancient magic.”

Series stars Alexandra Daddario, Harry Hamlin, Tongayi Chirisa, Betsy Brandt and Eliza Scanlen are joined by showrunner and executive producer Esta Spalding and executive producer Mark Johnson for a panel that features an exclusive sneak peek of the third season ahead of its 2027 premiere on AMC and AMC+.

Season 3 “picks up in Salem where danger looms over the witches, with Rowan Mayfair (Daddario) at the center of it. As ancient magic collides with new bloodlines, Rowan must wield her rising power and confront forces determined to control the fate of the witches.”

Friday, October 9, 5:15-6:00pm Main Stage

The cast and executive producers of The Walking Dead: Daryl Dixon discuss the fourth and final season of the series and debut some never-before-seen footage previewing the upcoming season. Panelists include executive producer and star Melissa McBride, showrunner and executive producer David Zabel, and executive producer Scott M. Gimple.

In the final season of the show, “while crossing the ravaged badlands of Spain, Daryl (Norman Reedus) and Carol (McBride) grasp onto hope – and each other – as uncertainty about their future grows.”

The Boulet Brothers’ Dragula: 10 Years of Terror Panel

The Boulet Brothers celebrate a decade of horror, filth and glamour, and open the crypt on the show’s upcoming seventh season. The brothers will be present for “an inside look at the making of their biggest season yet, stories from a decade of Dragula, and an exclusive first look at the new season.”

Shudder Is Here to Scare the S--- Out of You! Celebrating the Season of Screams Panel

Panelists including Ry Barrett (In a Violent Nature), David Dastmalchian (Late Night With The Devil), Ernest Dickerson (V/H/S/MIXTAPE), and Deborah Ann Woll (The Cycle) come together for a discussion on the current state of horror, what scares them the most, and the future of the genre, including exclusive first looks and what’s to come to the streamer.

For full coverage of New York Comic Con, be sure to follow IGN for all of the biggest news, announcements, and reveals when the event kicks off October 8.

articles.title: Starbucks Japan Is Getting a Massive Pokémon Collection — Including a Pikachu-Themed Latte
articles.summary: Starbucks has revealed a new Pokémon collection that will be coming to stores across Japan later this month.
articles.body:
Starbucks has revealed a new Pokémon collection that will be coming to stores across Japan later this month.

The collection, which follows Pokémon's 30th anniversary collabs with everything from Adidas to Krispy Kreme , will feature a Pikachu-themed latte as well as a new batch of merchandise. The full spread includes over 40 new products, ranging from tumblers and mugs to aprons, totes, and even gift cards.

While the Pikachu latte will only be available in person, select merch will also be offered through the Starbucks JP online store . Unfortunately, there’s no word on whether the collaboration will be available outside of Japan.

On September 30, Starbucks locations across Japan will debut the Pikachu Honey Cream Latte, a recipe selected through a nationwide competition that received over 700 submissions. The winning recipe was submitted by Junko Nitta of Starbucks Coffee Koriyama Asaka.

The latte is flavored with a mix of honey and caramel and colored after the electric Pokemon’s iconic yellow hue. Honey-flavored whip cream tops the drink, with red heart sprinkles mimicking Pikachu’s rosy cheeks.

The Pikachu Honey Cream Latte will only be available in a size Tall, retailing for around 690 yen (US $4.34). Some reports suggest the limited-time latte will only be available for as short as nine days, from September 30 to October 8.

Starbucks JP will also be releasing a line of tumblers, totes, aprons, and even new gift cards. The 41-piece collection will be a mix of online and in-store exclusives. Given ongoing stock and scalping concerns across all things Pokémon, Starbucks will reportedly be limiting transactions for the first couple days of the release.

Hikaru Ichijo provided 12 new illustrations for the collection, which show popular Pokémon enjoying pleasant moments and building friendships with their baristas. Even Pokémon need caffeine, I suppose. The featured Pokémon shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise, with most designs featuring Pikachu, Eevee, or one of the Gen 1 starters (Charmander, Bulbasaur, and Squirtle).

The illustrations are based on a collection of “stories,” which are themselves written on some of the designs. Some quotes include “Our adventure starts with a cup of coffee,” and “Crafting wonders with you.”

Starbucks is no stranger to collaborations, and North American stores will soon be getting their own limited-edition collection themed after the Peanuts franchise . Alas, that does not mean all is looking bright for the coffee shop giant. Starbucks also just announced that they will be closing 250 stores across North America by the end of the week, presumably part of the company's ongoing "Back to Starbucks" turnaround strategy.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: The End Times Begin: Total War: WARHAMMER III Unleashes Four New Legendary Lords
articles.body:
Strategy game Total War: WARHAMMER III has launched its biggest expansion yet, Lords of the End Times. A colossal collection of unique characters, deadly new units, and game-changing features inspired by one of Warhammer Fantasy's most cataclysmic events, it introduces four new Legendary Lords to Immortal Empires alongside a massive free update for all players.

For anyone unfamiliar, Immortal Empires is Total War: WARHAMMER's ultimate sandbox experience, combining the content of all three games in the trilogy into a single experience packed with legendary heroes, ancient rivalries, and globe-spanning warfare. As with previous releases, Lords of the End Times is available as a complete bundle with a 15% discount or as individual DLC purchases, allowing players to build their collection however they choose.

If you're new to Total War: WARHAMMER, there's never been a better time to join the action. In a first for the series, purchasing any part of Lords of the End Times grants access to Immortal Empires, even if you don't own any of the base games. That means a single purchase is enough to jump straight into the apocalyptic action and begin building your collection from there.

Leading the charge in Lords of the End Times are four new Legendary Lords, each arriving with their own unique campaign mechanics, playstyle, and legions of units. The most infamous of them is Nagash, the Supreme Lord of the Undead, whose ambition is nothing less than transforming the world into a vast Land of the Dead. An exceptionally powerful spellcaster, he can recruit units from across the undead races, giving players unique flexibility in how they build their armies and wage war.

Next up is Thanquol, the Skaven's most ambitious and accident-prone mastermind. Riding into battle atop his Rat Ogre bodyguard Boneripper, Thanquol specializes in deception, sabotage, and overwhelming enemies with vast armies of Skaven warriors. Players can enact elaborate Masterplans to outwit rival factions, conquer territory through cunning rather than honor, and unleash chaos across the campaign. However, things don't always go according to plan, so you'll need to be ready to deal with the unexpected.

The Glottkin are a trio of corrupted siblings who serve the Plague Lord, spreading disease and decay wherever they march. The scythe-wielding Otto and sorcerous Ethrac ride into battle atop their brother Ghurk, a colossal Chaos Spawn of mutated muscle. Together they combine physical and magical might as a single terrifying combatant. Their campaign revolves around corrupting the lands they conquer, transforming settlements into festering strongholds and slowly overwhelming enemies through plague, attrition, and relentless warfare.

Last but certainly not least is Boris Todbringer, the Elector Count of Middenland and one of the Empire's most celebrated warriors. Armed with his legendary sword Legbiter, Boris leads from the front, inspiring his followers and crushing enemies in close combat. Players can command soldiers from across the Empire, including newly added Middenland units and devoted followers of the wolf god Ulric, building armies focused on resilience, leadership, and the strength of steel and faith.

Lords of the End Times also arrives alongside one of the biggest free updates in Total War: WARHAMMER III's history. Crowning the update is Neferata, the Vampire Queen, a new Legendary Lord who uses secret vampire covens to manipulate rival factions from the shadows. Note that Neferata is only free to owners of Nagash or any Vampire Counts–related content.

Players can also look forward to major updates for both the Vampire Counts and Archaon the Everchosen, alongside three new end-game scenarios inspired by some of Warhammer's most infamous apocalyptic events. Updated victory conditions for every legacy Legendary Lord and a host of additional improvements round out a substantial free update for all players. Experience the cataclysmic world in the Lords of the End Times DLC on Steam now.
